name: Powdery Mildew
causes: High humidity, poor air circulation, temperatures between 60-80°F
treatment: Remove affected areas immediately. Apply neem oil or potassium bicarbonate spray. Improve airflow and reduce humidity below 50%.
risk_to_consumer: Inhaling mold spores can cause respiratory issues. Affected product should not be consumed.

name: Botrytis (Bud Rot)
visual_symptoms: gray or brown fuzzy mold inside buds
fluffy gray spores on bud surface
causes: Excess moisture, high humidity above 60%, poor airflow during flowering
treatment: Immediately quarantine and discard all affected buds. Cannot be treated — entire affected colas must be removed. Sanitize grow space.
risk_to_consumer: Extremely dangerous. Botrytis produces mycotoxins. Affected product must never be consumed.

name: Nitrogen Deficiency
visual_symptoms: yellowing of lower/older leaves starting from tips
leaves turning light green then yellow then dying
causes: Insufficient nitrogen in growing medium, pH imbalance preventing nitrogen uptake, overwatering
treatment: Apply nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Check and adjust soil pH to 6.0-7.0. Avoid overwatering.
risk_to_consumer: Does not pose a direct health risk but indicates lower quality and possibly underdeveloped buds.

name: Phosphorus Deficiency
visual_symptoms: purple or reddish discoloration on leaves and stems
causes: Low soil pH (below 6.0), cold root zone temperatures, lack of phosphorus in medium
treatment: Raise soil pH to 6.0-7.0. Apply phosphorus supplement (e.g. bone meal). Warm the root zone.
risk_to_consumer: No direct health risk. Indicates suboptimal growing conditions.

name: Potassium Deficiency
visual_symptoms: brown scorched leaf edges and tips
yellowing between leaf veins on older leaves
causes: Insufficient potassium, pH imbalance, excess calcium or magnesium blocking uptake
treatment: Apply potassium-rich supplement. Check and adjust pH. Flush medium if salt buildup is present.
risk_to_consumer: No direct health risk. May indicate harvested product has lower terpene and cannabinoid density.

name: Spider Mite Infestation
visual_symptoms: tiny white or yellow speckles on leaves (stippling)
fine webbing between leaves and buds
dusty or dirty-looking undersides of leaves
causes: Hot dry conditions, low humidity, introduction of infected plants or tools
treatment: Apply insecticidal soap, neem oil, or predatory mites. Increase humidity. Isolate affected plants.
risk_to_consumer: Mites and their waste on buds are contaminants. Heavily infested product should not be consumed.

name: Broad Mite Infestation
causes: Introduction via infected clones or tools. Too small to see with naked eye.
treatment: Apply spinosad or neem oil. Increase temperature temporarily to 45°C for 15 minutes. Replace heavily affected plants.
risk_to_consumer: Mite contamination on harvested product is undesirable. Affects taste and safety.

name: Heat Stress
visual_symptoms: upward leaf curling or cupping (taco shape)
brown or burned leaf tips and edges
bleached or pale yellow patches on top buds closest to light
causes: Temperatures above 85°F (30°C), lights too close to canopy
treatment: Increase airflow, lower temperature, raise lights. Increase watering frequency.
risk_to_consumer: Reduces terpene and cannabinoid content. No direct health risk.

name: Light Burn / Bleaching
visual_symptoms: white or yellow bleached areas on top buds
pale almost white upper leaves and calyxes
yellow or white coloring confined to areas closest to light source
causes: Grow lights too close to the canopy, especially high-intensity LEDs or HPS
treatment: Raise lights to recommended distance. Reduce light intensity if adjustable.
risk_to_consumer: Bleached buds have reduced cannabinoid content. Not a safety risk.

name: Calcium Deficiency
visual_symptoms: brown or rust spots on leaves
causes: Low calcium in medium, pH below 6.0, excess potassium blocking calcium uptake
treatment: Add calcium supplement (e.g. calcium-magnesium). Adjust pH to 6.2-7.0.

name: Magnesium Deficiency
visual_symptoms: leaves staying green along veins but turning yellow in between
causes: Low magnesium in growing medium, pH below 6.0, excess calcium blocking uptake
treatment: Apply Epsom salt (magnesium sulfate) foliar spray or soil drench. Adjust pH.

name: Root Rot
visual_symptoms: yellowing leaves that don't recover with watering
dark brown or slimy roots if visible
causes: Overwatering, poor drainage, pythium or fusarium fungi, lack of oxygen at roots
treatment: Improve drainage. Allow medium to dry out. Apply beneficial bacteria or hydrogen peroxide drench. In hydroponics, clean reservoir completely.
risk_to_consumer: Systemic fungal infection can affect bud quality and safety.

name: Overwatering
visual_symptoms: drooping leaves that are firm and puffy (not limp)
causes: Watering too frequently, pots without drainage, compacted soil
treatment: Allow soil to dry out fully before next watering. Improve drainage. Water less frequently.
risk_to_consumer: No direct health risk but reduces overall quality.

name: Windburn
visual_symptoms: clawing or downward curling of leaves
brown or dry edges on leaves facing airflow
causes: Fans blowing directly on plants at high speed
treatment: Redirect fans so air circulates without hitting plants directly.
